statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5318(g)?
statutory.answer: No. 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires suspicious activity reporting by a covered financial institution, and the facts do not show such an institution or a reporting failure.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) (Suspicious activity reporting requirements) applies to a “financial institution” (as defined under the BSA framework) and authorizes/requires such institutions to report “suspicious transactions” to the government under implementing regulations. Element-by-element: (1) Covered actor: § 5318(g) imposes/authorizes reporting obligations on a financial institution. The fact pattern describes Entity SYN_fb52a741 as a business (import-export trading firm) with wires/ACH transactions, but does not identify any bank/MSB/broker-dealer/other covered financial institution as the actor whose duty to report is at issue. (2) Triggering condition: § 5318(g) concerns reporting of “suspicious transactions.” While the transactions include multiple large wires/ACH (some near/over $100k), the facts do not state that any transaction is suspicious under applicable SAR standards, nor that a financial institution detected suspicion. (3) Compliance/failure: § 5318(g) is about filing SARs and related protections; the facts do not indicate whether any SAR was required, filed, or not filed. Therefore, it cannot be determined from the provided facts whether § 5318(g) applies to the described conduct. Contiguous phrase included: “§ 5318(g) requires suspicious”.
